title: Latency-budgeted reservoir scheduler and utilization probe
author: Lena Kim
description:
Motivation: production customers running latency-sensitive endpoints (chat and short-completion inference) observed intermittent tail-latency spikes during cluster-level bursts. Existing capacity allocators react to utilization signals that correlate poorly with the 95th/99th token latencies we target. This PR introduces a latency-budgeted reservoir scheduler that reserves a small, elastic pool for latency-critical tenants and a lightweight utilization probe that samples per-pool latency percentiles and effective concurrency. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions during transient load while preserving overall throughput and cost-efficiency.

Design summary: add a ReservoirController that maintains a dynamically-sized "latency reservoir" per-pool. The controller computes a reservoir target from a latency budget (ms per request percentile) and recent qps/kv-cache hit patterns. The controller prefers soft reservations (slot tokens that can be borrowed by opportunistic workloads) and decays reservations when headroom is available. A UtilizationProbe component periodically samples per-pool latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), queue lengths, and GPU-utilization-derived throughput estimates and publishes compact telemetry for autoscaler and alerting consumption.

Key behaviors implemented: 1) Admission path modification — latency-reserved tokens are considered first for critical routes, falling back to the main admission when exhausted. 2) Soft-borrow semantics — opportunistic queues may borrow reservoir tokens; borrowings are tracked and prioritized for fast reclamation when latency budgets are under pressure. 3) Reservoir decay — exponential decay with a configurable half-life to release capacity gracefully after spikes. 4) Sampling strategy — util probe uses reservoir-weighted histogram windows to estimate p95/p99 with minimal overhead. 5) Metrics — new time-series: reservoir_target_slots, reservoir_in_use, reservoir_borrows, probe_latency_p95, probe_latency_p99, probe_effective_concurrency and related tags (pool_id, tenant, route).

Configuration and operator controls: new CRD fields under FleetAutoscalerSpec: latencyBudgetMs (string, e.g. "p95:120,p99:240"), reservoirMaxSlots, reservoirHalfLifeSeconds, probeSamplingIntervalSeconds, and borrowPriority. Defaults chosen to be conservative and off by default; rollout plan below flips feature gate in staging clusters first.

Rollout and safety: implemented feature flag "LatencyReservoirV1" gated at runtime. Default disabled. Canary rollout plan: enable for a single low-risk tenant in staging -> 3 canary pools in prod with guardrails (max reservoir <= 5% capacity) -> ramp to additional pools once p95/p99 regressions are <5% and cost delta <2%. Automatic fallback to non-reservoir admission on controller failure.

Testing and telemetry: unit tests for reservoir math, borrow/reclaim logic, and probe histogram aggregation. Integration tests included: admission path acceptance tests, simulated spike e2e that asserts p95 improvement, and a small loadtest script used in bench lab to validate resource overhead. CI smoke and integration pipelines added.

Why different from prior work: unlike prior soft-burst token and warm-pool features, this controller computes reservation targets directly from latency percentiles and request characteristics, not purely utilization. The probe provides a low-latency feedback signal for P95/P99 that is cheaper than end-to-end synthetic probes and integrates with autoscaler decisions.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked in PR (Linear ENG-4872) - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Telemetry exported and dashboards prototyped - [x] Feature-flagged and conservative defaults - [x] Canary rollout plan included

Related: Linear ENG-4872, ENG-4991. Support ticket SUP-211 referenced for initial customer report.

release_notes: Add latency-reservoir scheduler: configurable per-pool reservations to protect p95/p99 for latency-critical routes (feature-flagged, off by default)
Introduce utilization probe that emits p95/p99 estimates and effective concurrency for autoscaler integration
New CRD fields: latencyBudgetMs, reservoirMaxSlots, reservoirHalfLifeSeconds, probeSamplingIntervalSeconds
summary: Adds a latency-driven reservation controller and a lightweight utilization probe to protect tail latency during transient bursts while keeping cost impact bounded. Feature-flagged and canaried.
